rules.title: Criminal-history inquiries, checks and disclosure
rules.requirement: Subject to the listed exemptions, rental housing providers must not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection or decision-making, or require disclosure or authorization for release of criminal history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley dealing with current or prospective tenants. The source lists exemptions for lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties with 1–3 units where an owner of record resides in one unit as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9; and units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates. The source does not supply the specific requirements for each exemption, so their application requires execution review.
rules.quoted_span:
The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106). An overview of the ordinance is available below. Please review the Ordinance for more specific details related to your property or tenancy.
It is unlawful to do any of the following with regard to current or prospective tenants
Inquire about criminal history
Indicate that persons with criminal backgrounds will not be considered for housing, including in rental advertisements, application materials, or verbally
Refuse to rent or terminate a tenancy based on criminal history
Require disclosure or authorization for release of criminal history

rules.title: Written notice and opportunity to respond
rules.requirement: A landlord taking any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history must provide written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords in Berkeley taking any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history, including refusing to offer a lease or refusing to add a family member. The source separately lists exemptions for lifetime sex offenders; limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions; owner-occupied properties with 1–3 units where an owner of record resides in one as their primary residence; units under rental agreements allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; and units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates. The source does not explain whether or how these exemptions affect the notice-and-response duty; that interaction requires execution review.
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond. This is due to the fact that criminal background checks and reporting services frequently provide inaccurate or incomplete information.

The source does not explain whether or how these exemptions affect formal notice distribution; that interaction requires execution review.

review.issue: The source describes current prohibitions and mandatory duties, supporting in_force status as of 2026-10-01. April 14, 2020 is identified as the Council passage date, not the effective date; all effective_date values remain null.
review.quoted_span:
The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106). An overview of the ordinance is available below. Please review the Ordinance for more specific details related to your property or tenancy.

review.issue: The substantive duties are supported, but exemption details are not supplied. Lifetime-sex-offender and public-housing/Section 8 exceptions must not be expanded into blanket exemptions beyond the source. Provider roles, criminal-history triggers, family relationships and several exemption conditions cannot be completely represented by the allowed facts; all extracted coverage therefore requires execution review.
review.quoted_span:
Exemptions
Please view the Ordinance on specific requirements for each exemption.
Lifetime sex offenders
Public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions
Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9
Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

review.issue: Separately located sanctions apply to any landlord found in violation of the Ordinance: administrative fines of $1,000–$10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; and injunctive relief. These details are retained here because the individual duty quotations do not also contain the sanctions. The source does not specify civil-plaintiff standing or further remedial conditions.
review.quoted_span: Any landlord found to be in violation of the Ordinance shall be subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

review.issue: The source identifies administrative complaint eligibility for applicants or tenants with criminal records who believe a housing provider violated their rights during application, leasing or tenancy, and for close family members in the described circumstances. This does not independently establish standing to bring a civil lawsuit.
review.quoted_span: Applicants or tenants with criminal records who believe their rights have been violated by a housing provider under the terms of the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance during the application, leasing, or tenancy process can file a complaint. Filing a complaint is also an option if you are a close family member of someone with a criminal record and you believe they were prevented by a housing provider from being added to your household on the basis of their criminal record, or from obtaining their own housing, or facing other adverse action from a housing provider.

review.issue: The termination rule is limited to criminal-history-based termination, subject to exemptions. This passage does not establish a universal just-cause eviction regime or a complete list of permissible termination grounds.
review.quoted_span: Refuse to rent or terminate a tenancy based on criminal history

review.issue: The notice-and-response duty is expressly stated, but the source does not specify response deadlines, required notice contents or how the listed exemptions interact with this procedural requirement.
review.quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.

review.issue: The distribution duty is supported, but the actual Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants is not reproduced. Its required contents and the application of exemptions to distribution cannot be established from this capture.
